subject: Evaluation clearance passport & acceptance tests — Medlytica MAP alignment
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara@medlytica.co>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Gupta <amit.gupta@medlytica.co>
Date: 2026-06-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Eval kickoff — defining success criteria and exit gates

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to lock down the evaluation scope and what "success" looks like before we spin up the pilot. Two asks from our side: (1) a concise MAP-style checklist that ties technical acceptance tests to business KPIs, and (2) explicit exit gates — the conditions that would cause us to pause or roll back.

Top-level context: Medlytica will run Redwood in a 6-week pilot integrated into our triage flow. Primary goals are improving triage throughput and reducing false positives on urgent cases. Business KPIs: +20% triage throughput, FPR <= 5% on urgent flags, and median inference latency <= 220ms end-to-end.

Can you send a short clearance passport (one-pager) that lists acceptance tests, measurement windows, data sets to use, and required evidence (logs, tracing, audit)? Also include any preconditions we should be aware of (e.g., data masking, retention settings).

Attaching a short RFP excerpt that lists current constraints.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lin
Head of AI Product, Medlytica
(sara@medlytica.co)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@medlytica.co>
Cc: Amit Gupta <amit.gupta@medlytica.co>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval kickoff — defining success criteria and exit gates

Hi Sara —

Great context — thanks. I put together a first draft of what I'm calling an Evaluation Clearance Passport (attached: MAP-draft-v1.pdf). High-level summary below so you can scan quickly:

1) Success criteria (quantitative):
- Throughput: +20% triage throughput vs baseline over a 2-week rolling window.
- Precision: urgent-flag false positive rate <= 5% measured across labeled holdout (500 cases).
- Latency: median end-to-end inference <= 220ms at 95th percentile request pattern.
- Stability: sustained error rate < 0.5% and KV cache hit rate >= 60% on repeated prompts.

2) Exit gates (stop/rollback triggers):
- Failure to meet any single quantitative threshold for 3 consecutive days during the pilot.
- A production-impacting regression in FPR that increases urgent incidents (customer-facing) by >10 events/day.
- Data-handling non-compliance (audit logs missing, KMS errors, or PII leakage) discovered during an evidence review.

3) Acceptance tests (evidence required):
- Automated smoke suite: 200 synthetic prompts covering common/edge cases (results: pass/fail and diffs).
- Labeled holdout evaluation: metrics CSV and confusion matrix for the 500-case set.
- Load test report: latency and tail behavior under expected peak QPS and 1.5x burst.
- Telemetry proof: sampled traces and token-level cost breakdown for representative endpoints.
- Security proof: SOC2 artifact pointer and KMS integration test logs.

4) Measurement windows and owners:
- Metric windows: daily aggregates with 2-week rolling checks; final decision after week 6.
- Owners: Medlytica — Product (Sara) for business KPIs; Redwood — Solutions (Marissa) + Eng (Ben) for telemetry & infra evidence.

5) Tactical recommendations (quick):
- Start pilot on reserved dedicated capacity for first 48 hours, then scale to target throughput.
- Enable prefix KV caching and warm cache with a 24-hour synthetic run.
- Add realtime alerts for FPR and latency spikes to the shared Slack channel.

Next steps: if you and Amit are aligned, we'll (a) drop the MAP draft into your shared Drive, (b) create the evaluation-tests.xlsx mapping each acceptance test to a Pass/Fail checklist and owner, and (c) schedule a 30-minute alignment call to finalize the sign-off gating cadence.

I attached MAP-draft-v1.pdf for review.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

On Wed, Jun 24, 2026 at 11:05 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> I put together a first draft of what I'm calling an Evaluation Clearance Passport (attached).

Couple of practical additions from infra/ops perspective:

- Performance thresholds: define soft vs hard thresholds. Soft threshold (warning) at 10% delta, hard at 20% (triggers rollback).
- Monitoring hooks: we should require sampling of request/response latencies with header-level tracing and an agreed retention (90 days).
- Canary plan: require a 24-hour canary at 10% traffic with an automated rollback policy tied to the exit gates. If the canary fails, we fail closed and stop ramp.
- Test artifacts: I'll drop evaluation-tests.xlsx into the Drive with exact test steps for smoke, holdout, load and security checks. It will include CSV templates and a small script to generate synthetic prompts.

I'll prepare the load test profile we used on a comparable customer and include the tail-latency graphs.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks team — this is heading in the right direction. A few priority clarifications from PM/security: 

1) Evidence for data governance: the acceptance tests must include a documented export of audit logs for a sampling window (we need request IDs and redaction proofs). If logs are incomplete or missing, that's an immediate stop gate.
2) SLA-band clarifications: if Medlytica requires a contract-level latency SLA, call that out now; otherwise we'll treat this as pilot-level SLOs.
3) Business signoff: final acceptance requires Product (Sara) + Legal (Medlytica) to sign the MAP acceptance document. Push to include a DocuSign link in week 5 to reduce friction.

Marissa — please add the data-governance checklist entry to the MAP one-pager and ensure the evaluation-tests sheet has the log export template. Ben — include retention policy and example trace samples in the Drive.

I'll be monitoring. If we hit any blockers with evidence collection, escalate to me and I'll coordinate with Engineering.

Neha
